messages.text: I put Maya's reading night on the shared calendar for the 12th. She asked if you were still coming with the peach cobbler bars.
Yes, I swapped my shift. Tell her I want to hear the whole paragraph, not the shortcut version.
You sound just like Dad at the old Ypsi kitchen table when Marcus tried to skip lines.
And Mom would tap that pencil twice and make us start over.
Rehearsal starts at 6:45 tonight. Pastor wants us to run the call-and-response part twice before the musicians come in.
I am leaving work now. Save my alto folder if Sister Mae has already set the chairs out.
I have it on your seat. Also Evelyn asked me if you remembered the homegoing committee list for Saturday.
Yes, I put Mama's notes in my tote. She still has Grandma's way of counting every pan and every name.
Are you still staying after choir to help Mrs. Lane with that little table by the fellowship hall?
Yes, just the sign-up sheet and some handouts about the city session Thursday. I promised I would keep it short.
Good. Put the youth center sheet on top. Folks will read that before they read any long city paper.
That is the plan. A few people asked me after Sunday what the badge-camera rule actually says, so I am bringing the plain-language copy too.
Did you still want me to save the last two tomatoes for your toasted bread pieces on Sunday?
Yes ma'am. I have basil left, and I am stopping for a fresh loaf after rehearsal.
Good. I also found the small foil pans you asked for, if the choir table still needs them.
Please hold those. Denise has me down for two pans and the tomato tray.
Baby, did you get in from work yet? Put the porch light on before you settle in.
Baby, did you see Sister Mae put the choir rehearsal change on FB? She said Tuesday is 6:15 now.
I saw it after supper. I marked it and took my name badge out of the Sunday photos before I added them.
I am in. Light is on, door chain set, and I put the phone on the nightstand.
Good. Call me before bed if the house feels too quiet after that late shift.
Good. Folks do not need every detail from your job showing. I liked the picture with the children by the fellowship table.
I will. I already made tea and there is only my plate in the sink, so cleanup is quick tonight.
That one is staying just for family and church folks. I am putting the phone down before the 10 o'clock headlines start running.
You still using those black work ones with the slick bottoms? I saw a sale by Briarwood.
I saw it too. I am letting this pay period settle first, then I will look again.
You still going to that township meeting tonight, or did the pothole on Hewitt finally win?
I am going. I circled the street repair line and the after-school gym item. Also want to hear what they say about rents by the Depot.
At least wear the newer pair when you do your laps after dinner. No hero moves on concrete.
That pair is already by the door for walking. The old ones are only getting me through short errands.
Ask them why every repair starts right after my tire gives up. And check if they mention those small shop grants Angela was talking about.
I put that on my card too. If they take questions, I am keeping it short and specific.
I laid out the blue-and-gold blocks again. The corner with your grandmother's apron strip is asking for one more row.
Save that corner for me. I want to bring the little notebook Mama found with the names written beside the scraps.
Good. Denise asked if we could leave two seats near the altos Sunday, so I told her I would check with you.
Tell her yes. I will bring my folder and the yellow tin.
Mama said the wreath from last year is faded. I can pick up a new one if you are working late.
I will get it after my shift. I already wrote the card and put Dad's small flashlight in the bag.
That little flashlight again. You know he would check the batteries before he checked the weather.
And fuss if I left without sweeping the car mat. I will be there by 10 Saturday.
You left choir with that tight look again. Did you hand off any of those potluck calls?
Not yet. I still have paper goods, Evelyn's ride for Friday, and the late shift schedule sitting on my notebook.
Call me before you start fixing every list by yourself. We can pick three names and move them off your page. 🙏
I almost typed something in the church group, then closed it. Easier to hear your voice for ten minutes.
Good morning, baby. Are you still taking me by the county office after my 10:30 appointment?
Yes ma'am. I checked Dr. Lewis's portal and the county page last night, so I wrote down the two questions for the nurse.
Thank you. Put that ginger tea in your bag too if your throat is still scratchy, and do not take extra tablets just because you are tired.
I packed the tea and honey. Only took the one dose from the bottle after breakfast, nothing more.
I found that copy of The Warmth of Other Suns on the library sale cart. Do you still want me to hold it?
Yes, please. I want to compare it with Grandma's story about the train up from Selma.
Bring that red-and-blue block too. The little suitcase print would sit nicely next to the church-step pattern.
I will tuck it in my bag with the book. Those pieces are starting to say more than I expected.
Mom asked if you found her little card from the clerk's office. She said you keep those papers in better order than all of us.
I put hers beside the stamps. Mine is on the kitchen table with the WEMU notes scribbled in the margin.
Of course you have margin notes. Did the slate mailer match what you heard this morning?
Mostly, but one county seat answer sounded too canned. I want to read the questionnaire before I fill anything in.
Did your mama get the new appointment time written down, or should I ask Keisha at the clinic to print it larger?
I wrote it on her yellow pad and put the referral sheet behind it. She already had me number the pages.
That sounds just like her. She used to have every permission slip and bell note lined up before anybody asked.
Yes ma'am. I am stopping by after work to make sure she didn't mix the morning bottle with the little white ones.
Are you still stopping at Depot Town before Mom's house, or should I grab something on my way?
I am going after I rinse these collards and peppers. If Ms. Laverne has the okra packs again, I will get two.
Get the small ones. Last time your freezer looked like a school supply closet.
That freezer saved me three dinners last week, so I am not ashamed.
You still need those two short stakes? I can drop them after Mom's grocery run.
Yes, please. The pepper starts are leaning again, and the tomato cage by the steps is acting tired.
That cage has one job and already needs a union break 😂
Leave my little setup alone. I already had my quiet half hour out there before the phone started ringing.
I can look at that slow tire leak Monday. Do not let the Belle Isle museum day eat the tire money.
I already moved the tire money back where it belongs. The little weekend envelope can wait until after the repair.
Good. Old car first, old buildings second. That is my professional mechanic speech 😂
You are not wrong. I just penciled the museum and that tasting room lunch for later in April.
Would Saturday the 14th still work for sewing, or did your board get changed again?
They moved me to 3 to 11 that day. I can come by Sunday after church if my eyes are not crossed from staring at those screens.
Sunday is fine. Bring the blue blocks, and I will make tea so you can rest them a little.
Thank you. I also have to finish a note bundle before I leave tonight, so I may be quiet until tomorrow.
I finished two more blocks. Do you still want the porch basket by the window when you sew tonight?
Yes, and I am putting on that Atlantic side with Lady Soul first. It keeps my hands from rushing.
That sounds just right. I always cut straighter when the old records are turning.
Tuesday's last verse is still in my ear too. Denise and I finally came in together.
Ma asked if you sat down after church or went straight into errands.
I did the Kroger run, but I used the small cart and skipped the far end of the lot.
Good. Also do not eat that ham twice in one day. Drink water and close the laptop by 9.
Yes ma'am. I have leftover greens with lemon, and I set the 20-minute timer for the computer.
Baby, did you write down what came out on Friday? I found one receipt from Kroger in my purse.
Did you find the old binder from your university classes? I remember it had those practice sheets you kept so neat.
Yes ma'am. I put Friday's numbers in the laptop file and copied the grocery line into the blue book.
I did. I borrowed the part where you make people explain the steps back in their own words.
Good. Keep your little envelopes straight before that school bill and the Visa both ask for their turn.
I already penciled both in. Nothing fancy this week after gas and your Tuesday ride.
That sounds like you. Just do not stay up all night making it perfect after that late shift.
I will stop after I add the clip notes. It actually fits this work better than I used to admit.
You still covering Mom's pharmacy run and choir setup tomorrow? That sounds like three people worth of Monday.
You still want me to look at that squeak before you pay the shop again?
I handed the paper goods to Denise and put Mom's ride on Angela's calendar. I was getting short over nothing.
Please. Last month's total hit about $3,100 after they fixed the car, so I am trying not to add another surprise.
Good. Eat something before you start fussing at the toaster too 😂
I can swing by after Mom's pharmacy run. If it is just a belt, I will save you from another dramatic receipt.
Good. My usual sheet sits closer to $2,800 or $2,900 when the car behaves and the home portal does not throw anything extra at me.
Already making soup. After that I'm playing Mahalia low and going around the block.
You still going to that field thing at the Y tomorrow, or did your knees vote no?
I packed my glove already. I am just doing the easy warmup and saving the longer walk for Tuesday morning.
You still want me to look over that packet from the break room? The one with dues and voting cards?
Bring it Sunday if you remember. My badge group is on a different page, but Jamal asked what I thought.
Good. And if you leave work late tonight, skip the sidewalk hero routine.
I know. Porch light is on and my shoes can wait until there is daylight or company.
Got it. Also don't forget to change that 401 thing before you fuss at me about budgeting again.
Already set the percent. I just need to check the payroll screen after this next check.
You see that score? I left the house at 3-1 and came back to foolishness 😂
I caught the last bit while icing my knee. Should have turned it off before the ninth.
Your knee talking because you tried to stretch a single into a double again?
It was a clean hit and you would have run too. I already took two from the little bottle and sat down.
Do you still have the burgundy strips in the clear shoebox, or did I bring those home by mistake?
They are here. Clear shoebox is under the cutting mat, right side. I put your paper template in there too.
Good. I will bring the cream squares. You can go straight from work if your shirt and badge are already waiting.
They are on the chair by the dryer. I just need to grab the shoebox and my small scissors pouch.
Did you ever make that one-page handout for the new folks, or did work swallow it again?
I have the first version. Camera blind spots, radio etiquette, who to call before guessing. I want it cleaner before I show Mr. H.
Good. And put your study hour on the calendar the same way you put choir on there. You will honor it if it has a box around it. 🙏
I did. Wednesday mornings for the thick blue book, then Friday I am asking about the next-step class he mentioned.
I found a block pattern that would frame those church picnic photos nicely. The one from Prospect Park looks like late 70s hair and everybody's Sunday best.
That sounds right. Mama says I was already being passed down the pews by then.
Bring the one with the blue bassinet next time. I can scan it at the library before we sew.
I will. Keep the Ypsi border idea too; that little water tower stitch made me smile.
The quilt shop sale ends Wednesday. Do you still want me to grab the batting if I go by there?
Hold off one more week. I paid the windshield man $412 this morning and moved it from the backup account.
That makes sense. We can use what I have here for Saturday and keep your list short.
Thank you. I also need to watch for those two acceptance emails and the little direct deposit before I loosen up.
They pushed tonight to 7:05. Ms. Linda wants our row early because that bridge keeps slipping.
I can make it if the floor lets me clock out clean. I have my gray folder in the car.
Good. Your low harmony is what holds that part together when the top line gets bright.
I marked the entrance after the hand clap section. Save my seat if I am walking in close.
Can you take Ma to the pharmacy tomorrow or are you already tied up?
Tomorrow is tight. I have to be at the community center by 4:20 with the folders for Jamal and Brianna.
I can do the pharmacy run. Those folders better come with snacks after all that prep.
Granola bars are already in my tote, along with the rough-draft checklist and the planner pages.
Sis, you watched that council replay yet? They had everybody on camera looking like they wanted dinner.
I watched the part I needed. The casino has enough rules for one hallway, so I listen close when the city talks about who checks whose paperwork.
That tracks. You like order, but you also like receipts.
Receipts and a place for young folks to go after school. Both would cut down on trouble before it starts.
Mama asked if you are making the rosemary and garlic bird for the 22nd or if I should order trays.
No trays. I already rubbed it down and put vegetables on my grocery list.
Fine, but I am claiming the corner with extra skin. Also bring that little cake if the choir ladies do not take all your baking energy.
I can do a small pound cake. The peach pan is for Denise's list this time.
Choir folder is in the alto pew. Also, Ruth said the library panel mentioned the millage again.
Thank you. I heard the same thing on Michigan Radio driving home, but I still want the county wording.
That sounds like you. You will not let a postcard do your thinking for you.
A postcard can point me, but it cannot have the last word. Especially not on local money.
Ruth said your triangles came out clean. Bring that steady hand Tuesday because the alto page turns are still a mess.
I can do Tuesday if I leave straight from Carla's desk. I promised the softball ladies I would answer about Saturday too.
One thing at a time. I will cover the paper goods, and you just bring your folder.
Thank you. I am putting Ruth's needle case in the bag now so I do not forget it.
Choir steps were a lot tonight. Did you wear the pair with the thicker inside?
Yes, and I kept the walking intervals short before rehearsal.
Good. Leave those thin-bottom ones for sitting work, not parking lot to sanctuary and back.
I know. I am stretching them one more month if the soles behave.
You got quiet after we held that long note tonight. You all right?
I was all right. When alto and soprano finally met, my shoulders came down.
Good. Go home, put your needle down, and let those records do the rest. ❤️
Already pulled the green sleeve from the crate. One side, then bed.
Good morning, baby. Did you cover those tender leaves before that cold air came through?
I did. I moved the basil close to the wall and tucked the greens under the old sheet.
That is good. Take those few quiet minutes before everybody starts needing you.
Already did. Coffee on the back step, no radio, just checking the pots.
Baby, are you home yet? I do not like you driving tired after those late hours.
Not yet, Mama. The floor team asked for another clip pull from Pit 4, and I need to attach my notes before I hand it over.
All right. Do it carefully, then call me from the car before you start driving, please.
I will. The badge door by the stairwell acted up too, so I am waiting for that entry to save.
Leaving Ann Arbor at 5:10. If Jordan asks, I did not forget the science board this time.
Good. I have the glue sticks and the $10 for his poster letters.
Look at us being responsible. Mom and Dad would not recognize the same two who hid report cards in the Ypsi hall closet.
Speak for yourself. I only hid one, and Grandma across the way still found it.
I can swing by Ma's at 7:20 tomorrow if you leave the pharmacy bag on the side table.
Thank you. The blue box is for Friday morning. The paper from Dr. Mason is tucked in the binder pocket.
Of course she has a binder pocket. That woman trained us with labeled folders before we could spell our names.
And she will still ask if you put it back in the right tab, so don't improvise.
I found the photo from the old Harriet Street picnic. Your grandmother is standing behind the quilt frame with Mrs. Delaney.
Please send it. I want to use those colors for the fellowship raffle piece.
Sending now. The library program on Saturday is saving two chairs for us after the choir luncheon.
Good. I can help serve plates first, then come over with Mama's notebook of names.
Mom said you offered to take both her lab ride and the church kitchen list. Why?
Because nobody had answered yet and I had the folder open already.
Send me the lab address. Do not put a whole speech in the family thread. Just call me after 3.
Thank you. I deleted the long text twice, so a call after 3 is better.
Mom's senior center packet asks for copies of any award letters or case numbers. Do you have anything like that for your household?
No, nothing to copy from my end. My rent folder just has the lease, DTE bill, water bill, and bank drafts.
For Mama's ride Thursday, I can cover pickup if you are doing that new-person shadow block.
Thank you. They gave me two people for the 10 to 2 block because I caught the table-pattern issue last month.
Good. I will mark your line blank and only bring Mom's papers.
Of course they did. You always notice the thing and then make a whole worksheet about it.
Please do. Also the Michigan acceptance came through, so I printed that page for my records.
The worksheet keeps them from just nodding at me. They have to mark what changed between clip one and clip two.
Maya can come Friday if that still works. I told her one small bag, not half her closet.
That works. I will clear the sewing baskets off the fold-out and put one towel in the bathroom.
She asked if she could leave her charger there.
Just for the night. I need my outlets back by Saturday because that room turns into quilt space again.
Are you still coming to rehearsal Tuesday, or did Thursday's sliding catch put you on the couch?
I am moving slow, but I will be there. I put the blue pack on my shoulder before bed.
Bring water and do not skip breakfast. Also check that bottle label before you mix anything with coffee.
Yes ma'am. I only used it last night after the game and kept it plain.
Did your ADP line clear yet? You sounded like you were waiting on it before choir potluck shopping.
It posted this morning. Stub says $4,600 up top, and the bank shows about $3,400 after everything came out.
Then paper goods only, Mildred. Let somebody else bring the trays this time. ❤️
I hear you. I already paid the home portal and utilities, so I am keeping the rest plain until next Friday.
Good morning, baby. I saw the school notice about people speaking Tuesday. Please do not let them take those children backward.
I am writing my three sentences now. The unit names the strike, the housing maps, and the women who organized lunches. That belongs in the packet.
Say it plain and keep your voice steady. Your grandmother used to say a covered wound still hurts.
I will. I am also asking why the clinic form table and registration table were moved to the hallway.
Did you put something aside before looking at those Toledo rooms? I know how pretty those old places can look online.
Yes, ma'am. The rainy-day transfer cleared this morning, and I only checked rooms after that.
That sounds like wisdom. If you go by the river, bring me a picture of the old mission marker.
I will. I marked the room price and the lunch place, but I am not paying until the March bills settle.
Found Dad's old work-order pad in a box at Mama's. Every line has a time, room number, and initials. Man did not believe in guessing.
Save it for me. I want the page where he wrote 'boiler room door sticks after rain.' That handwriting kept everybody honest.
He even wrote which screwdriver squeaked. I am sending you a picture before Angela tries to file it somewhere.
Good. I am closing my drawer at work the same way tonight: count twice, sign once, no shortcuts.
I saved you the blue batik strips. Are you still keeping Tuesday open, or did the casino schedule move again?
Tuesday is safe. I put in 8 hours through Kronos for Mama's appointment, and the balance still looks fine.
Good. Bring that envelope you mentioned if you want another set of eyes on the plan choices.
Thank you. I also want to ask you about that card Jamal passed around, since my department page is not the same as theirs.
Choir potluck list is almost set. Do you still want the June table by the fellowship hall window?
Yes, please. Mama likes to put the old Riverside picture there, and Angela already asked for peach cobbler.
I will save that spot. And I still say your family stories need their own tablecloth one day. ❤️
Only if it has a little map from the hospital side of town to the church. That is the whole Wilson route.
Good morning, baby. You answered late last night. Did you sleep enough after that shift?
Not enough. I woke up before five with my mind running through choir, your referral, and the dinner list.
Then do not add one more thing today. Say your prayer, take your walk, and let Angela bring the rolls.
I will. I put 11 to noon on the calendar with nothing in it.
I found your grandmother's cloth bag in the cedar chest. It has two church programs and that postcard from Cleveland.
Please save it for me. I am putting those dates beside the Wilkerson chapters so I do not mix up who left first.
Your grandmother would like that. She always said every stitch needed a name behind it.
That is why I want the names written before I finish the border.
Baby, did you find the referral paper from my blue folder?
Yes ma'am. It is clipped inside my planner on March 17, behind your ride note.
Thank you. Lay your work things out tonight too, since you have to pick me up early.
Already did the shirt, pants, badge, and black shoes by the laundry basket. I am putting your paper in my purse now.
Oil change place said your rear wiper is extra. Want me to bring one from AutoZone and save you the counter price?
Please. I only left a $30 cushion until the next casino hit clears on the 20th.
I got you. Your notebook probably has that wiper feeling judged already 😂
It does. I moved the Visa extra line down five dollars and marked it in the sheet too.
I saw Angela tagged you in that birthday album. You want me to tell her to take down the one by the valet sign?
Yes please. I am fine with the cake table ones, just not anything with the casino wall behind me.
Done. Also stop reading those late posts tonight. You got that early grocery run for Mama.
I know. I am checking the church event time once, then setting the phone across the room.
Mama said she heard you clear on that last response this morning. She is still talking about it.
Tell her I was trying not to overdo it. The new arrangement sits right in my comfortable range.
Comfortable or not, eat before you head to work tonight. And do not let them schedule you over Tuesday again.
I already blocked 6:30 to 8:30. If they need me late, they can ask somebody else first.
Choir table is covered. You do not need to bring a whole tray tonight.
I already cut up enough zucchini and greens for the week, so I can send a small pan with you.
Then keep it small. Also Auntie Nita's bean bowl sold out fast after service.
I saw that. I put her card in my purse for the next fellowship night.
Mom says you had her call the county nurse before she listened to Aunt Jean's Facebook post. I am glad somebody slowed that down.
I told her we can pray, make soup, and still ask the folks who keep the records.
Exactly. Also Marcus said you passed on wine at dinner again. You working late or just being sensible?
Early shift tomorrow. I had hot water with lemon and called it enough.
Our office copier jammed twice today. I saved some clean grade 7 organizer sheets if you still need them.
Yes, please. Thursday group ran out last week, especially the boxes for main point, details, and closing sentence.
I will put them in Ma's bag when I see her tomorrow. You can grab them before you head to the center.
That helps. They have one more regular week before break, and I want their folders ready.
Good morning, baby. Did you make your early appointment before the late shift tonight?
I did 25 minutes on the bike at the community center, then stretched before breakfast.
That is plenty. Take your breaks from that screen and do not let those casino hours steal your sleep.
I packed the blue-light glasses and soup from home. Alarm is set for bed when I get in.
I saw the parking lot was thin when choir let out. Did your Wednesday ladies wait for you?
No, they finished before I got there. I came home, did the video step routine, and stretched on the living room rug.
That was the right call. Tomorrow morning, ask one of them to meet you at Gallup if you still want the river path.
I texted Sharon already. If she cannot make it, I will just walk by the mall after breakfast.
Baby, did you mail my absentee envelope with yours, or are you taking them downtown after work?
I am taking both after my shift. I marked the city questions last night and put your envelope in my tote.
All right. I prayed over it this morning. Also, Mrs. Green asked what you told the young men at church about the summer work forms.
Tell her I will bring copies Sunday. They need those forms before the deadline, not another lecture.
Ang said you were about to cover Mom's groceries, the Sunday pans, and a double at the casino. That math is ugly.
I know. I made a note to check that work benefit number if I keep waking up at 4.
Good. Also text me the grocery list, not the whole family chat. I can grab Kroger after my U-M shift.
Calling you in five. The list is shorter when I say it out loud.
My rosemary made it through the cold snap. I can cut you a bundle before quilting on Saturday.
That would help. I used the last of mine in the soup pot yesterday.
I will bring it with the quilt blocks. Are you still taking cornbread squares to the choir room after we sew?
Yes, just one pan. Denise said someone else has the greens covered.
List for Saturday: Mom's pharmacy, Kroger, maybe shoe place if your feet survive that casino floor.
Pharmacy and Kroger first. The shoe place is only if the markdown table looks right.
Do not take the floppy pair for Mom's appointment. That hallway is too long.
I packed the firmer pair in the car. The floppy ones can wait at home.
List for Saturday: Mom's pharmacy at 10, council drop box by noon, then your flyer table at the union hall. Do not add six more errands.
Only adding the rent cap postcard stack and the street repair map. The hall table is just training signups and shift complaint forms.
Fine. Bring a thick marker. Those little boxes on city forms make everybody write like they are apologizing.
Already packed. I want the younger folks to know where to put their names before Monday.
Good morning. When you stop by, please bring the small frame from the cedar chest, the one with you three on the porch.
The porch picture from the Ypsi house? I know the one. Marcus has that crooked grin and Angela has the red barrettes.
Yes. Your father took it before Sunday service. I want to show the children how much everybody favored each other.
I'll bring it after I pick up snacks for them.
Did you call Mrs. Hattie about the van list for Sunday morning?
I did. She has three riders from Parkridge and one from near the old school.
Thank you. Your grandmother used to say you learn who people are by who they make room for.
I remember. I also confirmed the choir robes are back from the cleaners.
The library room is free on the 28th if you still want to spread the top out on the big tables.
Yes, please. My running group meets early that morning, so I can come over after I shower.
Bring the photo you showed me of your grandmother on the porch. That border needs that kind of memory beside it.
I will. Denise may ride over with me if rehearsal papers are done.
I sent you that IG strip-piecing clip and the basil planter idea. No need to answer while you are at work.
I saved both on break. That block would look nice with the green fabric from last month.
It would. Did you ever add the fellowship notice from Saturday to your page?
Yes, just the flyer and the quilt table photo, with the work shirt cropped out.
Mama says you borrowed the old photo of Granddad by the bus station. Are you framing it or sewing it into something?
Neither yet. I am laying it beside the Hamer book and the green scraps to see what belongs together.
Please make a copy before you start experimenting. You know I want one for my hallway.
I will scan it tomorrow. The station sign and his work shoes need to stay clear.
Daughter, please do not forget the fellowship hall list in the morning. They need paper goods counted before service.
I packed napkins, cups, and the sign-in sheets already. I will unlock at 8:15 and leave the kitchen cleaner than I found it.
Your daddy used to say a room tells on the last person who touched it.
I hear that every time I line up chairs. I will call you after choir.
You still coming by Ma's after work, or are you trapped with those binders again?
Coming by. I only need to print the camera tour pages and the quiz for the two new people on swing shift.
A quiz? You running a whole school in that back room now 😂
If they learn it right the first time, everybody's night gets easier. Then I can get back to my practice questions before dinner.
I can swing by with that outlet tester. You want me to knock or use the side key?
Knock first. The side key is only for family emergencies, and I keep it pulled from the hook unless somebody tells me they are coming.
Got it. Also, any bowls on the floor I should not step in? You know I trip over air.
No bowls, no toys, just my laundry basket by the washer. Watch that instead.
Mama asked if you are limping again or if Marcus was exaggerating.
He is exaggerating. I just chased one deep and felt it in my hip.
Mm-hmm. Put the uniform in the wash, take your two with something on your stomach, and go sit down.
Already done. I watched the highlights while the washer started and now I am off my feet.
Our clinic printed the new March sheet. I can bring you one to choir if you still want to compare it with Dr. Lewis's note.
Please do. The CDC page was clear, but I like having the paper copy for Mama's folder.
I will tuck it in my music bag. And for that cough, steam first, then call if it hangs on. You know the drill.
Steam pot is already on after lunch. I am not adding any extra cold pills tonight.
Baby, did you call about that Thursday paper? I put it beside the pill case so I would not forget.
Did you make it home from church all right?
I called before my shift. They moved you to 9:40, and I will come get you at 8:55.
Yes, Mama. The altos found their place tonight. I sat in the driveway a minute before coming in.
Good. I made a neat stack by the door. Old habits from the front counter never left me.
Sometimes you need that minute. Put on something old and warm, then get your rest.
That's the plan. The needle is already on and I am not touching the laundry basket.
I saw it. Folder, list, glasses, purse all in order. I will check the bottle question with you when I get there.
Did that glass place ever stop holding your card hostage?
Yes, it cleared. I am putting $50 back Friday and $50 after the next check until my cushion looks right again.
That is grown-folks math. I still say the windshield should have come with concert tickets.
Right. At least my March folder is done now: federal accepted, state accepted, and the small deposit already landed.

events.title: Wash, chop, bag fridge bins
events.notes: Use what is left from the backyard rows first. Check freezer space before buying from the Depot Town tables Saturday.

events.title: County Farm loop with A2WRC early crew
events.notes: Text Maya if parking lot looks empty. 10 min stretch after.

events.title: Water back beds before work
events.notes: Tomato cages, basil tray, rosemary pot. Pick only outer greens if they are ready.

events.title: Track loop before shift
events.notes: 3 min walk / 90 sec easy jog x 6. No hills. Pack water, reading glasses, and the unsalted almonds.

events.title: Payday transfers
events.notes: Rainy-day auto-transfer first. Then $35 to the gas/motel envelope for Fort Meigs or Greenfield Village. Check May room rates before buying admission.

events.title: Oakwood portal + DTE
events.notes: Confirm March ACH posted from checking; DTE and internet autopays scheduled. Update sheet after ADP deposit lands.

events.title: Evelyn - ride + question list
events.notes: Bring green folder, insurance card, pill bottles, and the paper with the noon-tablet question. She wants the forms clipped in order like her old attendance folders.

events.title: Blank block before errands
events.notes: Walk first, eat oatmeal, then call Denise before adding anything else to Saturday.

events.title: Work - camera room
events.notes: Check east-bank feeds after 7:00 changeover; finish write-up packet from Table 12 before clock-out.

events.title: Choir rehearsal
events.notes: Bring water bottle and old blue songbook. Put Lady Soul record on when home before cutting quilt squares.

events.title: Tuesday run-through
events.notes: Bring gray folder, black binder, and robe. Ask Denise about the measure 18 entrance on the lower line.

events.title: Read sample ballot + county clerk notes
events.notes: Compare school board and township items with Michigan Radio recap before choir texts.

events.title: Before bed
events.notes: Fill Tuesday boxes on planner page. Put black vest and white shirt on laundry-room hook. Move rosemary packets back to green caddy.

events.title: Before shift: badge-room walk-through with T. Reed
events.notes: Bring printed quick-start checklist; add ASIS book order and exam-fee estimate to March budget sheet after shift.

events.title: HR portal: March elections and deduction check
events.notes: Confirm Core PPO card mailing address, 401(k) match percent, and accrual balance before Friday. Print badge-class page for Jamal's question.

events.title: Revise Thursday walk-through packet
events.notes: Add two sample clips, three check-for-understanding questions, and space for the new hires to write what they noticed before I answer.

events.title: Riverside quilt notes and family records
events.notes: Bring Grandma Lottie's photos, 1978 clipping from St. John bulletin, and the old 734 address list for Ruth to scan.

events.title: Upload W-2 and state forms
events.notes: Check both accepted emails before moving $75 back to regular checking.

events.title: Blue room group
events.notes: Bring highlighters, two short passages, paragraph frame sheets, and blank planner pages. Ask Ms. Harris for the key.

events.title: Y pickup game - bring glove
events.notes: Pack cleats, water, knee sleeve, and the small drugstore bottle for afterward. Check score during warmups if service is decent.

events.title: City Hall listening session - notes card
events.location: Ypsilanti City Hall, 1 S Huron St
events.notes: Bring Denise's church sign-up sheet. Ask about camera-on timing, public complaint summaries, and where the youth jobs line sits in the spring budget packet.

events.title: Friday money pass
events.notes: Check CU app after work pay lands. Update March workbook tab and blue planner. Send $45 extra to Visa if grocery total stays under line.

events.title: Check Shoe Carnival clearance rack
events.notes: Try wide black pair after grocery stop. Compare against envelope amount; do not put on card unless marked down.

events.title: Oakwood stop, then Mama's ride
events.notes: Bring wreath, card, Dad's flashlight. Pick up Evelyn at 10:40 for church pantry boxes. Check trunk mat before leaving.

events.title: Fresh sheets for Maya's Friday stay
events.notes: Pull fold-out cover from hall closet; set one towel on chair; leave spare key under blue planter after 7:30 PM.

events.title: Ruth - blocks and binding
events.notes: Bring peach-thread spool, Grandma's note cards, and small scissors. Text Denise after about alto folder.

events.title: Early choir call, 10:30 service, fellowship hall cleanup
events.location: Second Hope on Harriet St., Ypsilanti
events.notes: Bring alto folder, white blouse, Mama's peach cobbler, and the envelope for the youth scholarship table.

events.title: Sunday dinner at Mom's - Marcus, Angela, kids
events.notes: Bring roasted chicken, spelling cards for Maya, AA batteries for Jordan's controller. Ask Mom where the old Harris Road photo album is.

events.title: Choir fellowship table setup
events.notes: Bring two foil pans, tomato tray, paper labels. Check oven space for Angela's greens before 1:45.

events.title: Quilt table with Ruth
events.notes: Bring peach scraps, Grandma Lottie's letter copy, Ida B. Wells book, and the Sunday choir recording Denise sent.

events.title: Phone tidy: albums, saved ideas, headline cutoff
events.notes: Post family dinner pictures after cropping casino lanyard. Save IG tomato stake reel and half-square triangle block. No headline tabs after 9:05.

events.title: Call HR line - ask about 3 free visits
events.notes: Only if the week keeps stacking up. Ask after Evelyn refill pickup and before casino shift.

events.title: Walgreens counter + 15-min wait
events.notes: Ask pharmacist about spacing from last fall card. Bring insurance card. Pick up Epsom salt and honey. No ibuprofen unless label timing is clear.

events.title: Library room: school board agenda review
events.location: Ypsilanti District Library, Whittaker Rd meeting room
events.notes: Bring printed questions: bus route funding, classroom aide cuts, book challenge list, and Feb. 24 notes from the curriculum packet.

events.title: Dr. Patel follow-up
events.notes: Bring cuff log, sleep notes, grocery sodium screenshots, and March walk/bike minutes.

events.title: Check-in with Mr. H
events.notes: Ask about fall class list, 2027 role map, and whether the new-hire checklist can become the standard packet for surveillance.

events.title: YMCA field practice, then garden beds
events.notes: Bring glove, knee sleeve, water. Stop at Lowe's for tomato cages and rosemary starts.

events.title: Work - day coverage
events.notes: Extra half-hour approved. Recheck card-reader report for service elevator; send final timeline to floor lead before 2:30.

events.title: Porch and quilt blocks
events.notes: After rehearsal: tea, lamp by the rocking chair, play 'I Never Loved a Man' side A low, no phone unless Mama calls.

events.title: Move $60 back to reserve
events.notes: After Treasury deposit posts; keep grocery debit and April rent draft separate.

events.title: County elections page: check drop box hours
events.notes: Confirm township clerk office hours; skim judges page and proposal explainer after NPR segment.

events.title: Stop at Evelyn's
events.notes: Check pill sorter, read the voicemail from Dr. Mason's nurse, and move Friday ride note to purse. Take her extra index cards; she asked for the lined ones she used for lunch counts.

events.title: Back step watering
events.notes: Rosemary pot dry. Thin greens. Check pepper tray before leaving for choir.

events.title: Porch and laundry shelf
events.notes: Put tomato stakes with seed tray. Refill plant tags. Check two white shirts before 4:30 shift.

events.title: Shadow block: pit-side review with Dana and Luis
events.notes: Start with what they would watch first, then compare their notes to my March 2 example. End with one question each before floor handoff.

events.title: Call HR before shift
events.notes: Ask why dental card has old apartment number. Confirm 16.25 available hours after Friday call-in. Check whether table-games petition is for their badge code only.

events.title: Center folders - last regular week before break
events.notes: Pack Angela's grade 7 organizer sheets, index cards, red pens, and timer. Start with chapter summary, then 10-minute folder clean-out.

events.title: Y league night
events.notes: Wear gray shirt. Bring glove, water, and flats for after. If shoulder acts up, take the usual two with food when home.

events.title: April route check
events.notes: Map Ypsilanti to Tabor Hill, Fort St. Joseph marker, and Niles motel. Compare gas estimate, admission, and one tasting flight. Hold off if cushion drops below target.

events.title: Payday split
events.notes: Confirm casino amount posted. Mark March 20 column: rent hold, Mom gas, groceries, campus-servicer $38, Visa $60. Copy final numbers to planner before leaving.

events.title: Friday money check
events.notes: ADP landed near $3,400. Move car line back to normal; March tracker target $2,850. Check Oakwood balance before choir.

events.title: Depot Town tables, then Parkridge food booths
events.notes: Bring small cooler bag. Look for basil starts, Auntie Nita's bowl, and $20 cash limit.

events.title: Wilson June 14 planning call
events.notes: Check cake size, ask Mama about the old St. Joe photo, and confirm whether the Ypsi High colors are too much for the napkins.

events.title: Quilting with Ruth
events.notes: Bring blue scraps, drink water, no extra errands after. If dinner prep runs long, text Angela for Sunday sides.

events.title: Drop off envelopes + church youth forms
events.location: Ypsilanti City Clerk drop box, 1 S Huron St; then New Hope Baptist fellowship hall
events.notes: Tote: sealed envelopes, marked sample sheet, 12 summer-work packets, copy of Thursday notes for Denise.

events.title: Section run-through

events.title: Return call from HR benefit desk
events.notes: Ask what the first appointment looks like. Do before calling Denise about choir handoffs.

events.title: Evening phone pass
events.notes: Check FB: Angela's potluck count, church cleanup time, Mama's photo comments. Check IG saves: cabbage recipe and border pattern. Put charger in kitchen at 9:35.

events.title: Reset front room after Maya
events.notes: Wash one guest towel; fold cover back into hall closet; move quilt frame from bedroom doorway to front room.

events.title: Try on black walking/work pairs
events.notes: Bring coupon, stand/walk the aisle before deciding. Use March leftover only; old pair stays for seated shifts if no good price.

events.title: Maya program, then meet Angela halfway
